Companion Animal Travel Desk Briefing

The Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps companion animal trips organized, safe, and clear for customers and the cabin team. New staff must move fast, read each request closely, and keep the passenger informed without extra noise. We handle cats, dogs, and other approved animals with the same steady process, so every file starts with complete details and ends with a clean handoff.

For booking, the deadline is 84 hours before departure, and late requests go to the supervisor for review. Confirm the passenger name, route, animal details, and contact method before you move the file ahead. If anything is missing, ask for it at once and keep the wording direct. Do not promise a space until the record is complete and the desk has confirmed acceptance.

For arrival pickup, use FM-394 and attach it to the file before release. Make sure the form matches the traveler, the pet, and the destination details, then pass the instructions to the next team without delay. If a passenger arrives with a change in pickup contact or location, record it in clear language and notify operations right away. Keep the exchange respectful, brief, and accurate.

You will also work with the cabin team, which monitors animals during flight and reports any concern that affects the handoff. If a traveler asks about the pet during the trip, answer with calm facts from the file and avoid guesswork. Yara Khan, Sana Moretti, and Millie are examples of the kind of family travel you may support, but the same standards apply to every case. Check the record, confirm the path forward, and keep each conversation professional.

What to remember is simple: complete the file early, use the right form, and keep every update clear.
